article_title: Docker Updates PHP Official and Hardened Images After the PHP2Shell Flaws, Moving the Four Supported Branches to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12

content_preview.title: Docker Updates PHP Official and Hardened Images After the PHP2Shell Flaws, Moving the Four Supported Branches to 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12
content_preview.summary: Docker says its PHP Official Images and Hardened Images were updated after CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619; the DHI refresh landed within 24 hours of the upstream patches.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Docker published a security update on October 22, 2026, saying it has refreshed its PHP container images after the two critical PHP flaws that the post calls "PHP2Shell." According to [Docker](https://www.docker.com/blog/security-update-on-php2shell-impact-for-docker-customers/), the company "updated the Docker Hardened Images and Docker Official Images on Docker Hub" and advises customers to update immediately. editor_notes.content_quality: Compact, well-structured 503-word Briefing (range 300-800) with Overview, What We Know, Guidance, a follow-up advisory section and an explicit What We Don't Know. Neutral tone, no AI self-reference, no promotional language.
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all three snapshots (gunzip, tag-stripped text) and re-fetched live. source-0 (docker.com blog, 'Posted Oct 22, 2026', Docker Security): live text identical to snapshot. Verified verbatim: 'we have updated the Docker Hardened Images and Docker Official Images on Docker Hub, and advise customers to immediately update'; 'Docker began tracking' on 'Tuesday, October 20, 2026'; 'a vulnerability in PHP itself, not in Docker's systems'; 'Docker Official Images have already been updated and released to Docker Hub and mirrored to Amazon ECR'; DHI moves 8.2.34->8.2.35, 8.3.35->8.3.36, 8.4.26->8.4.27, 8.5.11->8.5.12; 'completed and released within 24-hours of the upstream patches being made available'; 'Updating is the only complete mitigation path'; 'strongly recommend taking your system offline'; guidance attributed to Docker, the FBI and cybersecurity experts; affected incl. EOL 5.x, 7.x, 8.0, 8.1; both flaws described as request-memory management bugs. Docker's post does not mention CVE-2026-115560. source-1 (github.com/docker-library/php/pull/1694, checked via snapshot and GitHub API): title '[security] Update to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, 8.2.35', author jnoordsij (a community contributor, not Docker staff; PR body says they are not a maintainer), created 2026-10-21T13:44:58Z, merged 2026-10-21T14:19:23Z by LaurentGoderre; the PR bumps the version lines in the Dockerfiles (3 lines per file) and removes RC directories. The article's statement (opened by jnoordsij, merged Oct 21) is accurate and does not misattribute authorship to Docker. source-2 (php.net front page, live re-fetch matches): 21 Oct notice 'fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution' verified; 23 Oct 'Informational advisory: Session upload progress' verified: 'We suggest you set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, to fully protect from an unlikely RCE vector', 'unusual combination of configuration and application code' (page: 'under an unusual combination...'), full advisory for CVE-2026-115560 'with the next release'; 'PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project' verified. php.net gives no severity or CVSS for CVE-2026-115560 and the article states none. php.net notes the same setting was already a mitigation in GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp (CVE-2026-109619); the article omits this (minor, not misleading). suspicious_patterns null for all three. Allowlist: docker.com, github.com and php.net are all present by exact hostname (www. stripped); no edits needed. First-party framing: Docker is a vendor of Docker Hardened Images; the article attributes every Docker claim to Docker ('Docker says') and the DHI 24-hour claim is reported as Docker's statement; commercial context is not promotional. Independent sources: Briefing, no independence requirement; php.net and the GitHub PR are independent of Docker's commercial claims.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: Every number, date, version and quote checks against the snapshots. Key risk 1, 'PHP2Shell': Docker's post says the flaws are 'commonly known as PHP2Shell' and 'now commonly referred to as' it, and cites a PHP Foundation report; php.net does not use the name. The article body attributes it ('the two critical PHP flaws that the post calls PHP2Shell') but the headline uses it unattributed; the term is demonstrably in use (Docker blog URL/title, community GitHub references on the PR page) so the headline is acceptable, though the coiner is not identified by any source. Key risk 2: the Oct 23 CVE-2026-115560 advisory is accurately reported, dated correctly and clearly separated from Docker's update; the article explicitly says Docker's post (Oct 22) does not mention it and that the sources do not say how the images relate to it, so it does not imply coverage. One nuance: Docker does not enumerate Official Image tags; the 8.x tags in the headline come from Docker's DHI list and the PR title, and the article attributes each accordingly. Consistency with the published Herald Briefing (2026-10/22-php-8512-...): versions, CVE ids, unauthenticated RCE, and EOL branch statements are consistent. The internal link /article/2026-10/22-php-8512-8427-8336-and-8235-fix-two-critical-unauthenticated-rce-flaws-cve-2026-109618-and-cve-2026-109619 resolves to an existing published article and is described accurately as the report on the PHP security release. Body URLs equal article.sources (no orphans). No corrections needed.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral and factual; vendor statements consistently attributed.
editor_notes.originality: Justified, non-duplicative angle: the existing Briefing covers the upstream PHP release and advisories; this one covers Docker's image updates, PR #1694 and the later php.net informational advisory, none of which the earlier article contains. Different primary source (Docker blog) and new facts (DHI version moves, 24-hour claim, Official Images status).
concerns: Headline uses 'PHP2Shell' without attribution; the body attributes it to Docker's post, and no source says who coined it.
Article omits that php.net says upload_progress.enabled=0 was already listed as a mitigation for CVE-2026-109619 (minor omission).
recommendations: When using a nickname in a headline, attribute it or name the coiner if a source identifies one.
Note the Official Images are tracked in docker-library/php while the DHI list is Docker's own, to avoid blending two image lines.
editor_notes.overall_assessment: Accurate, well-hedged, properly attributed Briefing with a distinct container-image angle; all quotes verbatim, dates and versions verified, CVE-2026-115560 handled carefully. Ready for publication as-is. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate follow-up on container-image impact of a critical PHP flaw for a defined developer audience, secondary to the upstream coverage
